msg: no subject or device reference on this record — you cannot show whose consent it was. Add subject_id.
no collected_at on this record — a proof of consent with no moment attached proves nothing.
collected_at has no UTC offset. Write a full ISO-8601 instant such as 2026-06-01T08:00:00Z, not a bare local date.
consent is stored as one flag for everything. Consent must be specific: store purposes as a map with one entry per purpose.
no notice_version on this record, so nobody can say which wording the person actually read.
no notice_text_hash. A version string alone lets a rewritten page keep the old label; store a hash of the exact text shown.
this record was written with a purpose already switched on before the person acted. Pre-ticked boxes and silence are not consent.
no withdrawal_method recorded. Withdrawal must be as easy as giving, and you have to be able to show the route you offered.
no controller named on this record. A consent log shared between brands or tenants is unusable without it.
no expires_at on this record, so the consent is being kept as if it lasted forever.
this consent is set to run more than 13 months from the day it was given. Supervisory authorities treat 6 to 13 months as the outer edge.
this consent expired before today and is still being relied on. Re-ask or stop processing.
legal_basis on this record is not consent. Legitimate interest cannot be filed inside a consent log and called proof of consent.
a tc_string is stored without the cmp_id that produced it, so the string cannot be decoded back to a vendor list later.
